title: Adjectives I (Behaviour and Traits)
description: Find the precise words for personality, behaviour and attitude.

source.title: Advanced Grammar & Vocabulary — Express Publishing
source.note: Lesson vocabulary, examples and written tasks follow the supplied pages. Definitions are condensed for readability; spacing and obvious scan errors are corrected. Hints, explanations and model answers are study aids, not a publisher answer key.

lessons.title: Adjective position and connotation
lessons.body: The document marks negative connotations with (−), positive connotations with (+), and context-dependent connotations with (−/+). All these adjectives can be used before a noun or after it, often with the verb to be.

lessons.title: Curiosity, care and persistence
lessons.body: Inquisitive has two senses in the document: intrusive curiosity about private lives, and a positive eagerness to learn, especially in children. Meticulous stresses attention to small details; persistent stresses refusing to give up.

lessons.title: Temperament and reactions
lessons.body: Study the remaining traits and their examples from the document. Reckless and ruthless can describe actions as well as people. Use the character sketches in Practice to connect these meanings to evidence.

vocabulary.definition: Direct, even when the truth may hurt.
vocabulary.example: To be blunt, I think that what he did was cowardly and pathetic.
vocabulary.note: Context-dependent; not the same as merely brief.

vocabulary.definition: Loud and too confident in an irritating way.
vocabulary.example: That TV presenter is far too noisy and brash for my liking.

vocabulary.definition: Planning cleverly for personal gain without concern for others.
vocabulary.example: Percy is disliked by most of his colleagues because of his sly and calculating ways of getting what he wants.

vocabulary.definition: Showing little concern for other people’s pain.
vocabulary.example: His callous disregard of her feelings upset her.
Paul is not an easy person to have as a friend, because he is so cantankerous.
Why are you so cheerful today?

vocabulary.definition: So brief and abrupt that it sounds rude.
vocabulary.example: I knew from his curt tone that he was angry.

vocabulary.definition: Changing loyalties or preferences too easily.
vocabulary.example: How can you have trusted someone as fickle as Joan?

vocabulary.definition: Eager to learn, or too curious about private matters.
vocabulary.example: She was nervous. The man in front of her was being unusually inquisitive. / He is a very inquisitive child. He's going to love school.
vocabulary.note: Positive or negative, depending on context.

vocabulary.example: Mother was always meticulous about her appearance.
vocabulary.note: Often approving; can imply excessive care.

vocabulary.example: The customer was most persistent and refused to speak to anyone but the manager.

vocabulary.definition: Taking risks without considering the danger.
vocabulary.example: That was a very reckless thing to do. Do you realise you put your own life in danger?

vocabulary.definition: Prepared to act without mercy to achieve a goal.
vocabulary.example: The dictator was ruthless in silencing opposition and had the mass media strictly censored.

vocabulary.definition: Easily upset by blood or other unpleasant sights.
vocabulary.example: This horror film is not for people who are squeamish.
Rob sat in his room, in one of his sullen moods again.

vocabulary.definition: Willing to act dishonestly or immorally for gain.
vocabulary.example: He's probably the most unscrupulous businessman I've ever met. He'd do anything to make a profit.
We need someone who is calm, patient and level-headed. Joe is far too volatile.

vocabulary.definition: Quiet and unwilling to interact with others.
vocabulary.example: Katy is so withdrawn and introverted that you can hardly get a word out of her.

exerciseGroups.passage:
Bob,
Can you arrange a meeting with Joe Figgis? I think the three of us should get together. I've just received another script from him. It's terrible. I can't believe we are paying him to produce this kind of rubbish. Below is a copy of his character outlines, which should give you an idea of what the rest of the script is like.

SCARLET
Known as the Black Widow, she is beautiful and sophisticated. She is also poison. Driven by money and power, she will do anything to get what she wants. She lets nothing stand in her way. Everything is for the taking. Immoral, heartless and utterly unfeeling.

VANCE
Scarlet's right-hand man. Cold, cruel and callous. Steel blue eyes, steel cold heart. The man in black. A man of few words and no emotion, who shows no mercy. He is meticulous, efficient and dangerously loyal to Scarlet. He can neither understand nor tolerate weakness.

D'AVILA
Also works for Scarlet. Built like a truck, he is loud-mouthed, flashy and swaggeringly arrogant. He drips gold. He likes to take risks in every area of his life. Violent and volatile.

JANSEN
A rugged, handsome cop who is no longer the guy every cop wants for a partner. He keeps himself to himself, is curt and sullen. He doesn't seem to value his life anymore and often takes outrageous risks in his quest to discover the true identity of the Black Widow.

BONOMI
Thirty years on the force. A big man. A blunt man. He has seen it all. Only truly happy when he is shouting. He will argue for argument's sake. Known as Captain Outburst, he is in fact fiercely protective of his men. The booming voice behind the door.

LAURA HYDE
Young, blonde and beautiful. A crime reporter with the LA Mercury. Curious, and at times foolhardy. Always on the lookout for a ground-breaking story. Obsessed by the Black Widow, who is responsible for the disappearance of her brother. She will not give up until she finds the truth about the Black Widow and her story.

See what I mean? We must sort this out. Is 10 o'clock okay? Fax me to confirm.
Tony.
